project_specification.project_name: Scholium — public homepage at / with generative-engine optimisation
project_specification.addition_summary: Give the site a real front door. Today https://dev.scholium.fyi/ opens straight onto the paper feed; a first-time visitor never learns what Scholium is. This addition moves the feed to /papers (old /?tab= links redirect) and puts an Apple-grade marketing homepage at /, built from the approved design and copy reference docs/homepage/index.html: a Liquid Glass navigation bar, a hero with an illustrated paper-and-margin stage, sections for provenance (an interactive tamper demo), open review, AI pre-review, offline verification, roles, how it works, a comparison table, principles, the meaning of the name and an FAQ, all drawn with inline SVG and animated with spring physics (CSS linear() springs plus a small retargetable TypeScript spring), no images and no new dependencies. It also makes the site legible to search and answer engines (GEO): homepage JSON-LD (Organization, WebSite with SearchAction, WebApplication, FAQPage, DefinedTerm), ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD and Highwire citation_* tags on paper pages, robots.txt that welcomes AI crawlers in production, a sitemap of public pages and listed papers, and an llms.txt summary.

existing_context.stack: FastAPI API in apps/api (uv workspace, PostgreSQL in production, SQLite in tests); Next.js 16 App Router + TypeScript web app in apps/web (npm workspace), each feature owning a route group apps/web/src/app/(feature)/ plus apps/web/src/features/feature/; the paper feed is apps/web/src/app/(feed)/page.tsx at / with FEED_PATH = "/" in apps/web/src/features/feed/feed.ts; GlobalNav and the mobile tab bar live in apps/web/src/components/nav; the root layout wraps every page in SessionProvider and renders SiteFooter under it; the session token lives in browser storage, so server components cannot tell who is signed in (client components use useSignedIn from components/nav/session.ts); colour tokens in apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css (light default, dark via prefers-color-scheme, forced and scoped via data-theme="dark"/"light"); Source Serif 4 (roman and italic), Inter and JetBrains Mono are self-hosted via apps/web/src/styles/fonts.css; BrandMark and BrandLogo in apps/web/src/features/ui-kit draw the logo; resolveSiteUrl() in apps/web/src/app/site-metadata.ts gives the public origin from NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL; a root /opengraph-image already exists; no page emits structured data, robots.txt, sitemap.xml or llms.txt today
existing_context.test_baseline: unmeasured for this spec — the acceptance gate re-measures npm test at run start; Playwright journeys (npm run test:e2e) and system tests (npm run test:system) are outside npm test
existing_context.conventions: Feature code in apps/web/src/features/<feature>/ with colocated *.test.ts(x) and *.css.test.ts; never hardcode a hex in a component or feature CSS (read CSS custom properties from tokens.css); docs/design.md is the UI authority and docs/homepage/index.html is the homepage's design and copy reference; brand voice plain, precise, collegial, short sentences, no hype words; status is never colour alone (icon plus word)

feature.description: System serves the paper feed at /papers instead of /: the (feed) route group's page moves from apps/web/src/app/(feed)/page.tsx to apps/web/src/app/(feed)/papers/page.tsx with its behaviour unchanged (same server fetch, Latest, Reviewed and Following tabs, category and sort query parameters, Following fetched client-side) and its metadata title becomes "Papers"; FEED_PATH in features/feed/feed.ts becomes "/papers", so feedHref returns /papers for the default state and /papers?tab=reviewed for the Reviewed tab; GET /papers returns 200 with the seeded rows in the first HTML response; feed.test.ts and feed-route.test.tsx assert the new paths

UI displays the feed's tabs, category and sort controls with /papers URLs: the no-JavaScript selectors form submits to FEED_PATH (/papers) instead of /, tab links read /papers?tab=reviewed and /papers?tab=following, and changing a tab or category pushes /papers?… into the history; feed-page.test.tsx asserts these hrefs and pushed URLs

System redirects legacy feed links: next.config.js adds permanent (308) redirects from / carrying any of the feed's query parameters (tab, category or sort) to /papers with the same query string, so GET /?tab=reviewed returns 308 with Location /papers?tab=reviewed, while a bare GET / is not redirected and stays free for the homepage; next.config.test.ts asserts each legacy query redirect and the bare / case

UI displays the global navigation pointing at the feed's new address: the logo link's href becomes /papers (its accessible name stays "Scholium home") and the mobile tab bar's Home tab links to /papers and is marked aria-current when the path is /papers; global-nav.test.tsx asserts both hrefs and the current state on /papers

UI displays the dashboard's "Find a paper to review" action and the category page's "See the latest papers" empty-state action as links to /papers instead of /; dashboard-page.test.tsx and category-route.test.tsx assert the new hrefs

UI sends people who finish setting up to the feed: the onboarding form's finish redirect goes to /papers, its skip link and the verify-email page's continue link display with href /papers; the not-found and error pages' "Home" buttons and sign-out keep pointing at /, which becomes the public homepage; the existing onboarding and verify-email tests are updated where they assert the old target

System serves the web manifest (GET /manifest.webmanifest returns 200) with start_url /papers, so an installed app opens on the feed rather than the homepage; manifest.test.ts asserts start_url is /papers and every other field is unchanged

System keeps the browser and system tests on the feed: the Playwright journeys that open / to reach the feed (journeys.spec.ts and branding.spec.ts) open /papers instead with their assertions unchanged, and the system test's web entrypoint check also requests /papers and expects 200

UI displays the homepage's foundation and its first and last sections as components in a new apps/web/src/features/home, built from docs/homepage/index.html, the design and copy reference (reproduce its copy word for word, its layout and its motion); this feature adds no route (the assembly feature mounts the page at /), so its tests render the components directly. It delivers HomeNav, Hero, FactsStrip, Statement and FinalCta, the shared home.css, icons.tsx, reveal.tsx and spring.ts that the section features build on. (a) HomeNav: a sticky 60px bar with the BrandLogo lockup linking to #top, in-page links Provenance, Open review, AI pre-review, Verify and FAQ (hidden under 920px), and actions that follow the session via useSignedIn (signed out: Sign in to /signin and a filled Submit a paper to /submit; signed in: Browse papers to /papers and Your dashboard to /me); it is transparent at the top and becomes a Liquid Glass material once the page has scrolled past 8px (tint of --bg at 72 percent, backdrop blur 20px with saturate 180 percent and the -webkit- prefix, a 1px inset top highlight, a hairline and a soft shadow, fading in on opacity). (b) The hero: the pill eyebrow "Signed, open preprints and peer review", the h1 in three lines "The preprint, signed." / "The review, open." / "The record, kept." in Source Serif 4 semibold with the last word of each line in italic accent and tight tracking, the lead, the CTAs Submit a paper (/submit, filled capsule) and Browse papers (/papers, tinted capsule with an arrow that nudges on hover), the passkey fine print, and the illustrated stage: an aria-hidden mock paper card (Reviewed chip, "v3 · 3 versions", the id pill sch:k3f9-q2xz-7mwd/v3, title, authors, abstract with a margin-note highlight, a text-line skeleton, a small SVG calibration figure, and a badge that reads "Checking signatures…" then "Verified · signed by both authors · history intact") beside a margin column holding a Liquid Glass reader note that overlaps the card's right edge, a formal-review card with rubric pips and an AI pre-review card, described by an sr-only figcaption; under 900px the margin column stacks below the card. (c) The facts strip: Free to read and to publish; CC BY 4.0 by default; No token. No paywall.; Verifies offline, without us. (d) The "Why Scholium" statement, whose words ink in from --ink-3 to --ink as the paragraph scrolls through the viewport. (e) The final call to action: BrandLogo at 44px, "Your next paper deserves a margin.", the lead and the two CTAs; the homepage adds no footer of its own, since the root layout's SiteFooter follows the page. Motion follows the reference: the hero lines rise from behind a mask with a stagger, the paper card rises, the skeleton lines grow, the highlight sweeps, the figure's curves draw, the margin cards slide in on a spring and the badge's check draws, all as CSS keyframes whose easing is a spring curve written with CSS linear() (with a cubic-bezier(0.23, 1, 0.32, 1) fallback where linear() is unsupported); on a fine pointer wider than 900px the stage tilts toward the pointer (at most 4 degrees around y and 3 around x) on retargetable springs from a Spring class in features/home/spring.ts (response and damping parameters, semi-implicit integration with substeps, retarget mid-flight from the live value and velocity, settle detection); scroll reveal uses one shared IntersectionObserver exposed by reveal.tsx; icons.tsx holds the shared inline-SVG icon set from the reference. Every hidden start state in home.css is scoped under html[data-home-js] (the attribute the assembly feature's inline layout script sets before first paint), so with JavaScript off, and for crawlers, every word is visible. prefers-reduced-motion turns all motion into instant changes or short crossfades and leaves the statement fully inked; prefers-reduced-transparency makes glass solid; prefers-contrast adds 1px borders. The colour tokens the page needs and tokens.css lacks (an alternate section background, a skeleton-line colour, a strong margin-note, a glass tint and a glass highlight) are added to apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css for light, dark and forced dark, so no hex literal appears in features/home; no dependency is added. Tests cover the nav's signed-in and signed-out actions, the hero copy and CTA hrefs, that hidden start states exist only under data-home-js, the reduced-motion rules, the Spring class (it converges, a retarget mid-flight continues from the current value without a jump, damping 1 never overshoots) and that home CSS contains no hex literal

UI displays the homepage Provenance section (#signed) from the reference as a ProvenanceSection component in its own files (the assembly feature places it on the page; this feature edits no existing features/home file and keeps any icon it adds in its own files): eyebrow "Provenance", title "Signed by you. Checkable by anyone.", the lead, and the interactive tamper demo: three version blocks v1, v2 and v3 (date, fingerprint, previous fingerprint, "Signed by 2 of 2 authors" with a key icon) joined by arrows that draw in on reveal, and a tinted button "Change one byte in v2" (aria-pressed, aria-controls the demo) that swaps v2's fingerprint bafy…q2xz for bafy…9e7c with a spring crossfade, shakes v2 once and outlines it in --critical with the line "Signature no longer matches", turns the v2-to-v3 arrow dashed in --critical with an ✕ badge that pops in on a spring, marks v3's previous value with a ≠, and switches an aria-live verdict from "Verified. History intact, signed by every author." (check icon, --verified) to "Verification failed. v2 no longer matches what its authors signed." (✕ icon, --critical); pressing it again (now labelled "Restore v2") puts everything back; under 860px the chain stacks vertically with downward arrows. Below it: the three points (Your key stays yours; Every author agrees; A stable ID to cite, with sch:k3f9-q2xz-7mwd/v1 in monospace) and the "Corrections are part of the record." row with the five status chips Preprint, Under review, Reviewed, Corrected and Retracted, each an icon plus a word in the app's chip colours, popping in with a stagger. Tests cover the toggle in both directions, aria-pressed, the live verdict text and that every chip carries its word

UI displays the homepage Open review (#review) and AI pre-review (#ai) sections from the reference as OpenReviewSection and AiPrereviewSection components in their own files (the assembly feature places them; this feature edits no existing features/home file). Open review: eyebrow, title "Peer review, out in the open.", the lead, and a bento grid (six columns on desktop, one column under 980px) with the wide tile "Structured, not starred." holding an example rubric (Soundness 4, Evidence 4, Reproducibility 3, Novelty 3, Clarity 5, Limitations 4, five pips each whose filled pips scale in on a spring with a row-and-column stagger, the values as n/5, Confidence High, Recommendation Minor revisions, exposed as role img with the full text equivalent), the tile "Sealed until it's fair." whose two report cards (Reviewer A, Reviewer B) show Committed with closed locks and, 1.4 seconds after coming into view, open their shackles on a spring, switch to Revealed in --verified and fade their redacted lines in, and three small tiles (Anonymous, still accountable; Authors answer back; Discussion with manners) each with an icon in an accent-tinted rounded square. AI pre-review: a two-column split (one column under 900px) with the eyebrow in --ai with the sparkle icon, title "A careful first read, within about an hour.", the lead, three points, and an example AI panel with the fixed banner "Advisory. Generated by AI agents. Not a peer review." and three findings (agent name in --ai, the finding in serif, an evidence link, a confidence bar that fills on reveal, and Rebut, Confirm and Wrong pills) that rise in with a stagger. --ai appears only in the AI section. Tests cover the banner text, the rubric's text equivalent and the sealed reports' change of state

UI displays the homepage Verify band (#verify), Who it's for (#who) and How it works (#how) sections from the reference as VerifyBand, RolesSection and HowItWorksSection components in their own files (the assembly feature places them; this feature edits no existing features/home file). The Verify band is a dark section that sets data-theme="dark" on its own element so it uses the dark tokens in both themes, with eyebrow "Verify anywhere", title "Take the record with you.", the lead, an example terminal (role img with a text label) whose command "scholium verify reward-calibration.car" types in with a stepped width animation and a blinking caret and whose checklist lines (Signed by all authors (2 of 2); History intact (v1 → v2 → v3); Files match what the authors signed; Timestamp anchor pending; No retraction; Verified.) fade in one by one, three link cards (Check a file in your browser to /verify; Export what you cite to /papers; See the network to /network) that lift on hover and press in on pointer-down, and a note tagged "Planned": Public timestamp anchoring, DOIs and independent library nodes. Who it's for is a WAI-ARIA tabs segmented control (Authors, Reviewers, Readers, Libraries; Arrow Left and Right, Home and End move focus and selection; roving tabindex) whose white indicator slides and resizes between tabs on the Spring class (response 0.4 s, damping 0.8) and whose panels hold the reference copy and CTAs (/submit, /papers, /papers, /network); all four panels are in the server HTML and only client code hides the inactive three. How it works shows the four numbered steps (Sign in; Submit; Get listed; Gather the margin) with connector lines that draw on reveal, horizontal on desktop and vertical under 900px. Tests cover keyboard navigation of the tabs, aria-selected and hidden states, each panel's CTA href, that the server render contains all four panels, and the terminal's text label

UI displays the homepage Compare (#compare), Principles (#principles), Name (#name) and FAQ (#faq) sections from the reference as CompareSection, PrinciplesSection, NameSection and FaqSection components in their own files (the assembly feature places them; this feature edits no existing features/home file). Compare: title "Same free preprints. A record you can check.", the lead, and a semantic table (sr-only caption, scoped row headers, columns "A typical preprint server" and "Scholium", the reference's seven rows, the Scholium column tinted with a check icon per cell) that becomes labelled two-column rows under 720px. Principles: the reference's title and its four cards No token., No paywall., No verdicts. and No quiet edits. with the reference text. Name: an animated brand glyph beside a dictionary entry; BrandMark gains an optional animated prop that only adds part class names (page, line, strip, bracket) and changes neither its geometry nor its default output, and on reveal the page fades and scales in, the lines grow left to right with a stagger, the strip grows downward and the bracket slides in on a spring; the entry shows dfn "scholium", "/ˈskoʊ·li·əm/ · noun · plural scholia", the definition "An explanatory note written in the margin of a scholarly text." with a margin-note rule, and the lead. FAQ: an "at a glance" card (a definition list of the reference's eleven facts, sticky on desktop) and the reference's eleven questions as native details and summary elements with each question as an h3 and a plus icon that turns 45 degrees on a spring when open, opening with an animated height where ::details-content and interpolate-size are supported and instantly elsewhere; the questions and answers live in features/home/faq.ts as plain data in the reference's exact words so structured data can reuse them. Tests cover the table's semantics, that BrandMark's default output is unchanged, that the animated prop adds the part classes, and that every FAQ entry renders its question and answer

category.name: Homepage Assembly and Generative Engine Optimisation

feature.description: System serves the full homepage at / (GET / returns 200, statically prerendered, no API call) and publishes its metadata and structured data: a new (home) route group (apps/web/src/app/(home)/layout.tsx and page.tsx, with no GlobalNav and no mobile tab bar) mounts HomeNav and home-page.tsx; the layout's first child is an inline script that sets data-home-js on html before first paint, which arms the animations' hidden start states; home-page.tsx renders the sections in the reference's order (hero, facts strip, statement, Provenance, Open review, AI pre-review, Verify, Who it's for, How it works, Compare, Principles, Name, FAQ, final call to action) and index.ts exports them; the (home) page's metadata sets the absolute title "Scholium — signed, open preprints and peer review" (not the "%s · Scholium" template), the reference description, a canonical URL for / resolved against the site URL, and Open Graph and Twitter summary_large_image cards that use the existing /opengraph-image; the page renders one application/ld+json script whose @graph holds Organization (name, url, logo /brand/icon-512.png at 512x512, description), WebSite (alternateName "Scholium Network", inLanguage, publisher, and a SearchAction whose target is /search?q={search_term_string}), WebPage (isPartOf, about, dateModified), WebApplication (applicationCategory ReferenceApplication, isAccessibleForFree, an Offer at price 0, publisher and the reference's featureList) and DefinedTerm "scholium", plus a FAQPage built from features/home/faq.ts so its questions and answers always equal the visible ones; every URL is absolute and comes from resolveSiteUrl() in apps/web/src/app/site-metadata.ts, never a hard-coded domain; the JSON is serialised with every less-than sign escaped so no string can close the script element. Tests check the section order in the rendered page, parse the JSON-LD, check each @type, that the FAQPage entries equal faq.ts, that the canonical and every URL use NEXT_PUBLIC_SITE_URL, and that a less-than sign in a string is escaped. Playwright journeys in apps/web/tests/e2e/home.spec.ts then check the whole thing in a real browser: / displays the h1 lines and both CTAs, and following Browse papers lands on /papers with the seeded papers listed; /?tab=reviewed redirects to /papers?tab=reviewed; the "Change one byte in v2" button flips the verdict to "Verification failed" and "Restore v2" flips it back; the role tabs switch panels with the arrow keys; an FAQ question opens to show its answer; the page's JSON-LD parses and contains FAQPage and WebSite; with reduced motion emulated every hero line is visible at once; with JavaScript disabled the hero, the statement and all four role panels are visible; /robots.txt, /sitemap.xml and /llms.txt answer 200 with text/plain, an XML type and text/plain; a seeded listed paper's page carries citation_title and a ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD block; the page has no horizontal scroll at a 375px viewport; and a load budget holds: the HTML document for / is under 150 KB uncompressed, the page requests nothing from any other origin, and the h1 is present in the first HTML response

System serves robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt for crawlers and answer engines. apps/web/src/app/robots.ts: in production (NODE_ENV production and SCHOLIUM_ENV production) it allows every user agent, names GPTBot, OAI-SearchBot, ChatGPT-User, ClaudeBot, Claude-SearchBot, Claude-User, PerplexityBot, Perplexity-User, Google-Extended and Applebot-Extended explicitly with the same rules, disallows the private paths /me, /mod, /consent/, /review/, /onboarding, /recover, /verify-email and /ui-kit, and points to the sitemap; outside production it disallows everything for every agent. apps/web/src/app/sitemap.ts lists /, /papers, /search, /verify, /network and /policies, one /c/{category} entry for every category in the site's category list (components/nav/categories.ts), plus the newest publicly listed papers from the papers API (paged, at most 5,000 entries, each /p/{id} with lastModified from its newest listed version), never unlisted, held or tombstoned ones, and still returns the static entries when the API is unreachable. apps/web/src/app/llms.txt/route.ts answers GET /llms.txt with content-type text/plain; charset=utf-8 and the markdown in docs/homepage/llms.txt (title, one-line blockquote summary, the key facts, the pages list and the name), with every link absolute and built from resolveSiteUrl(). Tests cover the production and non-production robots output, the sitemap's static and category entries, its filtering and its fallback when the API fails, and the llms.txt content type and absolute links

System publishes scholarly metadata on paper pages so search engines and answer engines can identify and cite them: for a publicly listed paper, paperRouteMetadata adds a canonical URL (/p/{id} for the newest-version page and /p/{id}/v{n} for a version page) and Highwire Press citation tags through Metadata.other (citation_title; one citation_author per author, in author order; citation_publication_date and citation_online_date from the version's listed date as YYYY/MM/DD; citation_abstract; citation_pdf_url when the version has a public PDF; citation_publisher "Scholium"; citation_language "en"), and the paper page renders one application/ld+json ScholarlyArticle (headline, name, abstract, author as an ordered list of Person with name and, where the profile shows it publicly, an ORCID sameAs; datePublished and dateModified; identifier as a PropertyValue with propertyID "sch" and the sch: id; url; license; isAccessibleForFree true; version; publisher Organization Scholium; creativeWorkStatus set to the paper's status word: Preprint, Under review, Reviewed, Corrected or Retracted), with every URL absolute from resolveSiteUrl() and every less-than sign in the JSON escaped; unlisted, held, tombstoned and unavailable pages emit none of it and keep robots noindex. Tests cover the full tag set for a listed paper, author order, a retracted paper's status, the version page's canonical, and that tombstoned and unavailable pages emit no tags and no JSON-LD

System documents the homepage in docs/design.md: §4 Information architecture shows Home (the public front door) at / and the Papers feed at /papers, with the legacy /?tab=, /?category= and /?sort= links redirecting to /papers; a new subsection under the screens describes the homepage (its sections in order, docs/homepage/index.html as the design and copy reference, the motion rules: springs as CSS linear() curves and a retargetable TypeScript spring, transform and opacity only apart from the highlight sweep and SVG stroke drawing, and the reduced-motion, reduced-transparency and contrast behaviour) and the GEO surfaces (homepage JSON-LD, paper-page citation tags and ScholarlyArticle, robots.txt that welcomes AI crawlers only in production, sitemap.xml and llms.txt); the handbook in docs/handbook is not changed by this feature

project_specification.integration_points: The (feed) route group moves from / to /papers (apps/web/src/app/(feed)/papers/page.tsx, FEED_PATH in features/feed/feed.ts) with legacy query redirects in apps/web/next.config.js A new (home) route group owns / and renders apps/web/src/features/home, inside the root layout's SessionProvider and above its SiteFooter; section features add their own component files and one assembly feature places them in home-page.tsx GlobalNav (components/nav) points its logo and the mobile Home tab at /papers; HomeNav reads the session with useSignedIn BrandMark in features/ui-kit gains an optional animated prop for the homepage's name section New colour tokens in apps/web/src/styles/tokens.css (light, dark and forced dark) resolveSiteUrl() in apps/web/src/app/site-metadata.ts is the single source of absolute URLs for canonical links, JSON-LD, robots.txt, sitemap.xml and llms.txt paperRouteMetadata and renderPaperRoute in features/paper-page/paper-route.tsx emit citation tags and ScholarlyArticle JSON-LD New App Router metadata routes apps/web/src/app/robots.ts and sitemap.ts and the route handler apps/web/src/app/llms.txt/route.ts
project_specification.constraints: docs/homepage/index.html is the homepage's design and copy reference: reproduce its copy word for word and its layout and motion; where it conflicts with docs/design.md brand rules or tokens, docs/design.md wins. Neither docs/homepage/index.html nor docs/brand is modified The homepage makes no API call and no external network request: fonts come from the self-hosted apps/web/src/styles/fonts.css (no Google Fonts), icons and illustrations are inline SVG, and there are no raster images in features/home No new runtime or dev dependencies (no GSAP, no Motion, no animation library); springs are CSS linear() curves plus the small Spring class in features/home/spring.ts No hex literal in features/home components or CSS; every colour reads a CSS custom property from tokens.css, and new tokens are added there for light, dark and forced dark Every word of the homepage is in the server-rendered HTML and visible without JavaScript; hidden animation start states apply only under the data-home-js attribute set by the home layout's inline script Animate transform and opacity only, except the hero highlight's background-size sweep and SVG stroke-dashoffset drawing; honour prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-reduced-transparency and prefers-contrast; touch targets at least 44px on touch; visible focus rings on every control; text contrast at least 4.5:1, including through glass The logo is drawn only by BrandLogo and BrandMark with the delivered geometry and token colours; no shadows, gradients, glows or recolouring on the mark Copy claims only what the Phase 1 product does today; anchoring, DOIs and independent nodes are labelled Planned; no hype words Absolute URLs come from resolveSiteUrl(); no domain such as scholium.fyi is hard-coded in apps/web Unlisted, held and tombstoned papers never appear in the sitemap, in JSON-LD or in citation tags robots.txt allows crawling only in production; every other environment disallows everything The feed's behaviour, query parameters and data are unchanged apart from its path; existing links to /?tab=, /?category= and /?sort= keep working through permanent redirects All existing tests (npm test) and Playwright journeys (npm run test:e2e) stay green; update a test only where it asserted the feed at / or the old hrefs
